posts.text:
Colombia’s presidential election is heading to a stark runoff. In the first round, right-wing Abelardo de la Espriella led Petro’s left-wing heir. De la Espriella is no classical liberal, but a victory for him would mark a sharp rejection of Petro’s legacy and Latin America’s long left turn, writes Cato’s Marcos Falcone.
ow.ly/VLie50Z78Of

If Massachusetts wants lower rents, the answer is removing barriers to more housing supply, not rent control. The voters rejected rent control in 1994 and should reject it again, argue @jeffreyamiron and Jonah Karafiol. 

ow.ly/Mf5J50Z6QM5

The Declaration's promise rests on a simple idea that William Blackstone gave the Founders: rights to life, liberty, and property are inherent by nature, and government exists only to protect them. Restoring that birthright means less government and more freedom, says Cato’s James A. Dorn.
ow.ly/Aww950Z78zy

The Fed’s post-2008 toolkit quietly blurs the line between monetary and fiscal policy. By paying interest on reserves, the Fed can buy more assets without immediate inflation pressure—making “backdoor” deficit finance easier. Cato’s @NorbertJMichel & @JaiKedia warn this is a fiscal time bomb.

ow.ly/4k7H50Z6Lke

Almost 1 out of every 9 dollars the federal government spent on SNAP was lost to improper payments in FY2025.  
 
OBBBA made states bear part of the cost of SNAP payment errors. Now, amid Farm Bill debates, some senators want to delay those requirements. That would be a mistake, say Cato’s @RominaBoccia and Tyler Turman.

ow.ly/hjLV50Z6TPk

Overdose deaths are falling, but the decline is difficult to square with claims that the drug war is working. Evidence points instead to harm reduction, changing patterns of drug use, behavioral adaptation, and the fading effects of the COVID era. Cato's Jeffrey Singer, MD, explains.

ow.ly/G2sG50Z6Hrr
Please join us for a discussion with @RandyEBarnett on his new memoir, Felony Review: Tales of True Crime and Corruption in Chicago: nitter.net/i/broadcasts/1wxWjjmXw…

The SEC tracks virtually every trade and investor in America through a massive financial surveillance system that Congress never clearly authorized. It acquires billions of records without warrants or suspicion. 

A $150M+ surveillance machine with no clear legal mandate should be shut down. Learn more from @Thomas_A_Berry and Kimberly Coleman.  
ow.ly/nnca50Z6H6L

By most any measure, the United States has the most expensive health sector in the world. 

Removing government barriers to new providers would expand patient access, increase choice, and help make health care more affordable. 

Cato scholars propose immediate, supply-side policy changes that would broaden choice and improve affordability. Check out the Cato Institute Handbook on Affordability: ow.ly/YZeZ50Z5BJ1

Companies use personalized pricing to offer discounts — not to gouge you. Banning it doesn't protect consumers, it limits competition, distorts prices, and makes markets less efficient. The result? Higher costs for everyone, say Cato's Christopher Gardner and Juan Londoño. 

ow.ly/SVby50Z6P3G

The Supreme Court’s Callais decision signals that drawing districts with race in mind is now legally hazardous, whether the goal is minority representation or not. In a new Cato Podcast episode, @Thomas_A_Berry and @walterolson unpack the ruling, the crossroads between the 14th and 15th Amendments, and why a simple compactness rule could solve most of this if Congress had the will.

Listen on Apple, Spotify, and our website!

Apple: ow.ly/SjQi50Z6ntL 
Spotify: ow.ly/woxM50Z6ntJ 
Website: ow.ly/1

A new USPS rule would put the Postal Service in charge of validating and rejecting mail ballots, a procedure states already do and have built up over years. With the election five months away, expecting USPS to rebuild that system in weeks is a recipe for problems.

ow.ly/AQm050Z6HlO

Government equity stakes in private firms invite favoritism and corruption. When Washington becomes a shareholder, companies focus more on political access and less on creating better products. That's a patronage system, not free enterprise, explains Cato’s @DeHavenTad.
ow.ly/OMs850Z6GwM

Every year, the Bank Secrecy Act forces financial institutions to file 28 million reports on ordinary Americans — at a cost of $59 billion. The return on that massive invasion of privacy? Only 275 IRS investigations. It’s time to fix it, says Cato's @EconWithNick. 

Learn more: ow.ly/pq0o50Z4W2H

Video

A criminal justice system should focus on one core job: protecting the public from dangerous people. That means shrinking the criminal code that punishes conduct that poses no genuine harm to others while ensuring that violent offenders stay behind bars, explains Cato’s @foxmike90.
ow.ly/jvRf50Z6H8k

The IEEPA tariffs were illegal. Refunds are legally owed. Yet the Trump administration announced that it will appeal a court order to refund all importers the $166 billion it collected. 

Cato's @AlfredCObregon says using procedural hurdles to deny importers their legally owed refunds should not be allowed. 

ow.ly/uRU650Z6GBR

Not only is birthright citizenship enshrined in the United States Constitution by the 14th Amendment, but it has also greatly benefited the US economy, explains Cato’s Michelangelo Landgrave. A new study estimates the economic impact of birthright citizens’ incomes to be $7.7 trillion.
ow.ly/lAk350Z6p6O

23 states already allow qualified foreign-trained doctors practice in the US without repeating residency. California has a chance to catch up — and patients in underserved communities will be better off for it, says Cato’s @dr4liberty.

ow.ly/vXUS50Z5mUX

South Carolina's license plate reader network captures nearly 150 million observations a year. 99.8% have no known connection to criminal activity. That's not law enforcement — that's mass surveillance. 

Cato filed an amicus brief urging the Court of Appeals to foreclose this surveillance apparatus.

ow.ly/s1To50Z6hal

What if you could design your dream job? At Cato, you can.
 
You propose the job. Cato funds it. We make it happen together.
 
Learn more and apply: ow.ly/SWMp50Z6krr
